observation_summary: The Joda-Time library fails when performing date arithmetic that crosses the year 0 boundary (which does not exist in the Gregorian/Julian calendar systems), throwing an IllegalFieldValueException because the internal logic does not correctly account for the missing year 0 when transitioning between positive and negative years.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves modifying the internal calculation logic within the GJChronology class to explicitly check if the resulting year is 0 or less during date arithmetic and adjusting the instant by subtracting an additional year to skip over the non-existent year 0. This is a correction to the computational procedure (the algorithm for adding years/weekyears across the cutover) rather than a simple guard or initialization error.
evidence_used: The fix_diff_oracle shows the addition of logic to check if the year is <= 0 and then adjust the instant by calling .add(instant, -1) to skip the year 0.
The failing tests indicate that the system is incorrectly landing on year 0 or failing to correctly transition across the year 0 boundary.
The stack traces show the error originates in the chronology's arithmetic methods (e.g., GJChronology$ImpreciseCutoverField.add).

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix adds conditional checks (if year <= 0), these are not merely guards to prevent an error; they are part of the core arithmetic logic required to correctly calculate the date across the year 0 boundary.
The fix is a local procedural correction to the arithmetic logic within existing classes, not a design-level capability omission.
